$comment: SvelteForge module metadata contract (#236, capabilities #323). Each module declares its identity, capability contract (requires/provides/optional) and files. Capabilities are validated structurally at install time by @svforge/addon-kit — a project satisfies them with the SVForge template or its own implementation.

ui.skeleton.title: Skeleton v5 design system
ui.skeleton.description: Skeleton theme wiring (design tokens, presets) so Skeleton-styled components render correctly

ui.svforge.title: SVForge base UI kit
ui.svforge.description: the canonical component structure (src/lib/components/svforge: primitives/, ui/) and shared utils such as cn()

i18n.messages.title: Paraglide message catalogs (FR/EN)
i18n.messages.description: Paraglide i18n with messages/{locale}.json catalogs so modules can merge their UI copy without inventing keys

auth.currentUser.title: Authenticated user (locals.user)
auth.currentUser.description: an authenticated user is available in server locals (Better Auth in SVForge) so endpoints can enforce identity

auth.admin.title: Admin role helpers ($lib/server/admin)
auth.admin.description: role helpers such as isAdmin() guarding admin-only routes

database.drizzle.postgres.title: PostgreSQL via Drizzle ORM
database.drizzle.postgres.description: a Drizzle client on PostgreSQL (src/lib/server/db) so modules can register their schemas in the barrel

storage.object.title: S3-compatible object storage
storage.object.description: an S3 client wiring (endpoint, bucket, credentials) for persistent object storage

runtime.longLivedWorker.title: Long-lived worker runtime
runtime.longLivedWorker.description: a runtime that keeps a background process alive (in-process runner) — serverless platforms terminate it

runtime.websocket.title: WebSocket-capable runtime
runtime.websocket.description: a runtime that allows keeping WebSocket server connections open — serverless platforms terminate them

base.description: UI kit, layouts, theme, SEO, Paraglide FR/EN, Vitest baseline

deployment.$comment: Deployment profiles (#332). The declared profile lives in the project .svforge.json (deployment.profile, default node-long-lived); npx svforge doctor warns when an installed module is incompatible with it. This block mirrors @svforge/addon-kit (DEPLOYMENT_PROFILE_INFO + MODULE_PROFILES).

node-long-lived.title: Long-lived Node server
node-long-lived.description: an always-on Node process: background timers and WebSocket servers live in the same process as the app
examples: adapter-node on a VPS or container
systemd service behind a reverse proxy

serverless.title: Serverless functions
serverless.description: short-lived, request-scoped functions: no background timer survives the request and no WebSocket server can be held open
notes: use a connection pooler (Neon, Supabase pooler, PgBouncer) and set DATABASE_RUNTIME=serverless so src/lib/server/db uses the serverless-safe client

edge.title: Edge runtime
edge.description: edge isolates (V8 workers): no long-lived process, no WebSocket server, and no raw TCP sockets — Node drivers do not run there
notes: postgres.js opens raw TCP sockets: the SVForge database stack needs an HTTP-driver replacement SVForge does not provide

separate-worker.title: Serverless app + long-lived worker
separate-worker.description: the web app runs serverless while background jobs and the WebSocket server run on a dedicated long-lived Node deployment of the SAME codebase
examples: Vercel app + worker container running the same image
notes: only the worker deployment runs the job runner / WS server; web replicas set JOBS_WORKER=web so they never start one

notes.edge: postgres.js opens raw TCP sockets, which edge isolates do not allow — run the app on Node (long-lived or serverless) or replace the DB driver with an HTTP-driver implementation

notes.serverless: the in-process runner is killed between requests — use the separate-worker profile: a dedicated long-lived worker deployment (JOBS_WORKER=worker) polls the queue while web replicas set JOBS_WORKER=web
notes.edge: no long-lived process and no raw TCP sockets — run the worker on Node (separate-worker profile)
notes.separate-worker: the runner lives ONLY on the dedicated worker deployment (JOBS_WORKER=worker); web replicas set JOBS_WORKER=web and merely enqueue

notes.serverless: function instances cannot hold WebSocket servers open — use the separate-worker profile: hub.listen(PORT) on a dedicated long-lived Node/WS server, with the app publishing through a shared backend (e.g. Postgres LISTEN/NOTIFY) or HTTP calls to that server
notes.edge: no WebSocket server and no Node net stack — run the WS server on Node (separate-worker profile)
notes.separate-worker: run the WS server on the dedicated worker deployment via hub.listen(PORT) — SvelteKit serverless adapters never expose the underlying HTTP server
